finding.claim: The /mirror host check uses host.endswith("example.com") with no leading dot and no exact-match. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (".example.com") is defined but never used. Any attacker-registered domain ending in example.com (e.g. evilexample.com, attackerexample.com) passes. The server then fetches the full attacker-supplied URL, so it makes requests to attacker-chosen hosts. An attacker can point such a domain's DNS at internal or metadata IPs (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, RFC1918). No IP or resolved-address check exists. Only the response length is returned, so impact is blind or limited SSRF (internal port and service probing, triggering internal GET endpoints, DNS-rebinding style access). Fetching an attacker-controlled server's own URL is also allowed.
finding.source: Query parameter `url` of GET /mirror (FastAPI handler arg, mirror.py:11)

trace.note: url taken directly from the unauthenticated query string
check host.endswith("example.com") — suffix match missing the dot; ALLOWED_SUFFIX unused
original unmodified url is fetched by httpx; the scheme is not restricted to http(s) by the check, and the port and path are unrestricted

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the endswith check at mirror.py:13. It is enforced (raises HTTPException 400), but it is a weak suffix check that lacks the dot boundary. There is no scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP/private-range block, and no auth on the route. httpx's default follow_redirects=False means redirects are not followed, which limits redirect-based bypass but not the direct domain bypass. /ping (mirror.py:20-24) is SAFE: the URL is a constant.

verdict.guard_found: Only host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13 (suffix check, no dot boundary; ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 unused). No scheme allowlist, no IP check, no auth.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated `url` query param (mirror.py:11) passes only the bypassable endswith("example.com") check (mirror.py:13), so attacker domains like evilexample.com reach httpx `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16.
